correctness.rationale: Under Haar, y and v=y+x+f_eta(y) are independent because (x,y)->(y,v) is an invertible affine torus shear in x with Jacobian one. Rewriting x0 and x2 in these coordinates separates the two-time Fourier integral, and the exact two-branch integration gives J_eta(m,r) for all integer frequencies, including its removable cases. J_eta(0,k)=0 for all nonzero integer k because tent f_eta sends Haar to Haar, proving uniform wrapped displacement. Two nonzero modes, K(1,-1)>0 and K(1,2)<0, prove dependence and linear eta onset; the cat-map endpoint is independent because X2=2X0+3Y0 and 3Y0 is Haar. The TV lower bound follows from the bounded-character inequality. An independent checker passed 398 comparisons, but the infinite result rests on analytic proof.

originality.rationale: Original 2021/2022 open full text gives the family and Bernoulli mixing windows; the inspected theorem and calculations do not state the new evaluated all-parameter two-step Fourier law, independence boundary or nonzero sum-difference signature. Distinct two-tent-shear literature and accessible claim overlaps were compared by implication, not titles alone. Remaining risk of unpublished/unindexed harmonic derivations is acknowledged.
residual_risks: A complete search of all specialist shear/Fourier literature and unpublished calculations was not possible; exact general Fourier integrals could be derived elsewhere without matching title or terminology.

The author thesis Mixing in the Presence of Non-Monotonicity (University of Leeds, 2022), https://etheses.whiterose.ac.uk/id/eprint/32186/1/Thesis_final.pdf, was identified but not examined in full; it could contain short-time moment calculations.
The 2005 Cerbelli–Giona endpoint paper was referenced through the primary article rather than fully inspected; an endpoint-only computation would not itself imply the all-interior-parameter result.

The two-tent-shear paper and 2023 decay paper were assessed only from abstracts; their full texts were not read for hidden comparisons. Their described maps differ from the present one-tent-one-linear family.
Published findings index is not exhaustive; a failed search is not publication-priority proof.

value.rationale: This parameterized area-preserving map is a mathematically motivated model of laminar mixing with nontrivial open mixing questions. The result gives the complete measurable two-step coordinate joint Fourier transform throughout the family, not a numerical slice, and detects a genuine diagnostic blind spot: uniform first and second circular displacements coexist with nonindependent time-separated coordinates. The sharp endpoint classification, strictly positive lowest sum harmonic and linear onset of unequal-frequency dependence quantify the contrast, while the formula is reusable for trigonometric observables. The question is a natural statistical invariant and is not merely a routine restatement of Haar invariance or Bernoulli mixing.
